**Randersklyngen** is a healthcare cluster (sundhedsklynge) operating within [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] in Denmark. It serves as a local organizational unit evaluated in the national quality monitoring programs for the treatment of [[atrieflimren|atrial fibrillation]], as detailed in the annual "Atrieflimren i Danmark" reports published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) and Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut.

The cluster is notable for its clinical performance across several quality indicators. Randersklyngen successfully meets the national standard for Indicator 1, which measures the timely initiation of anticoagulation therapy for newly diagnosed patients, achieving a result of 93.5% [^src1]. In the context of [[indikator-8|Indicator 8]], which tracks the provision of structured patient education within the first year of diagnosis, the cluster is noted as being quite close to fulfilling the national standard, reaching a rate of 42% [^src5]. 

Furthermore, Randersklyngen is consistently included in national and regional benchmarking analyses. It is mapped on geographic distributions for the incidence of ischemic stroke ([[indikator-5|Indicator 5]]) alongside other clusters such as [[aarhusklyngen|Aarhusklyngen]] and [[midtklyngen|Midtklyngen]] [^src4]. The cluster's data is also tracked across multiple supplementary analyses—including treatment coverage over 1-, 2-, and 5-year periods, annual P-creatinine measurements, severe bleeding incidents, heart failure, and mortality rates—providing a comprehensive view of its cardiovascular care quality [^src2] [^src3] [^src6] [^src7] [^src8]. Recent 2025 reporting continues to monitor the cluster's performance across these indicators, tracking metrics such as treatment coverage, severe bleeding, and mortality [^src9] [^src10] [^src11] [^src12].
